_comment: Baselines for scripts/perf_gate.sh. The emitter (scripts/emit_perf_latest.py) picks a row count (100K smoke by default, --rows N or PERF_NUM_ROWS for the nightly job), writes tests/perf/latest.json with a `scale_key` set by that row count, and the gate consults the matching section of `scenarios_by_scale` below. Per-scale ceilings are NOT interchangeable — absolute query latencies don't scale linearly with row count. New scales must add their own section here.
production_targets_comment: v2.0 success-criteria (cleanup_plan.md §Success criteria — concrete): cold_path_36M_1h_iceberg_committed_p95_ms ≤ 2800, warm_path_36M_1h_p50_ms ≤ 1900. Validated separately via scripts/loadtest_generator.py + scripts/dev/loadtest_probe.sh against a representative dataset; not measurable inside a GitHub Actions runner.

smoke_100k._comment: PR-blocking smoke gate on every push. 100K rows × 7 query runs in ~2s wall. Catches gross regressions (extra GROUP BY, accidental cross-join, SELECT * inside a hot lookup) and constant-factor explosions. Misses superlinear-only regressions because constant-factor overhead dominates at this scale — those are caught by mid_500k + nightly_1m.

mid_500k._comment: Optional mid-tier gate. Invoked via PERF_NUM_ROWS=500000 — covers the 10× inflection gap between smoke_100k (constant-factor-dominated) and nightly_1m. Seed values are interpolated halfway between the bracketing tiers; refresh with measured headroom-padded numbers after the first real CI run, same procedure as the other tiers. Wire into ci.yml as an opt-in PR job (label or path-pattern triggered) for query-shape-touching changes.

nightly_1m._comment: Nightly + on-demand gate at 1M rows. The 10× scale-up from smoke surfaces superlinear regressions (extra n-ary join, missing index, O(N log N) instead of O(N)) that the 100K smoke can't see. Numbers are headroom-padded over the 2026-06-16 emit; refresh both this section and the emit when a legitimate improvement drops the floor. NOT a production target — see production_targets_comment.

notes: Emitter: scripts/emit_perf_latest.py (--rows N or PERF_NUM_ROWS env var). Gate: scripts/perf_gate.sh.
CI runs the smoke variant on every PR (.github/workflows/ci.yml). The nightly_1m variant runs from .github/workflows/perf-nightly.yml on a cron schedule + manual workflow_dispatch.

The 50% threshold gives room for runner-to-runner variance (~20-30% at 100K, tighter at 1M because constant overhead dominates less). Catches a 2-3× regression that indicates a real cold-path problem.
If a synthetic-data improvement legitimately drops the numbers further, refresh the relevant scenarios_by_scale section AND (optionally) tighten the values to keep the gate biting.
